title: Which program envelopes a water utility's requests break

blocks.text: A city water utility (a fictional one) collects capital requests from three programs: water mains, treatment plants and meters. Each request starts in a year and spends a profile of amounts ($k) in that year and the following ones. Finance has already set an **envelope** for some programs and years: the most that program may spend that year. Before anything is selected, the capital planning team wants to see where the requests already break an envelope.

items: `requested_by_year(requests, programs, years)`: for every program in `programs` and every year in `years`, what the requests would spend there if all were funded as asked. Every program and year appears, with 0 where nothing is asked. Spend in a year outside `years` is left out.

`oversubscribed(requests, envelopes)`: one tuple `(program, year, requested, excess)` for every envelope that the requests exceed, with `excess` the amount above the envelope, sorted by program and then year. An envelope met exactly is not exceeded.

blocks.text: A request for a program not in `programs` (or with no envelope) is left out. Before you code, take a request that starts in 2027 with the profile (500, 300, 100) and write down what it adds to 2027, 2028 and 2029. The tests use small hand-made request lists. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from envelopes import Request, oversubscribed, requested_by_year

reqs = [Request("P1", "pumps", 2030, (200, 100)), Request("P2", "pumps", 2031, (250,)),
        Request("R1", "reservoirs", 2030, (500, 500, 300))]
years = [2030, 2031, 2032]

table = requested_by_year(reqs, ["pumps", "reservoirs"], years)
print("pumps by year:", table["pumps"])
print("reservoirs by year:", table["reservoirs"])
envelopes = {("pumps", 2030): 300, ("pumps", 2031): 300, ("reservoirs", 2030): 450, ("reservoirs", 2032): 400}
print("over the envelopes:", oversubscribed(reqs, envelopes))

cases.says: requests are totalled by program and year, with zero for an empty cell
every envelope the requests exceed is listed with its excess, in order
a request worked over several years counts in each of them, not all in its first
requests exactly equal to their envelope do not break it
a program nobody asked for still appears, with a zero in every year
